exponentialGeneralArgument.reason: a^x is positive. a^h-1 is positive for a>1 and negative for 0<a<1. Multiplication by negative b reverses the sign. This proves all four regimes, whereas checks at two inputs do not.
exponentialGeneralArgument.limits: For a>1, a^x tends to 0 as x tends to -infinity and to +infinity as x tends to +infinity. For 0<a<1 the directions reverse. Multiplication by negative b preserves approach to zero from below and turns unbounded positive values into unbounded negative values.
boundaryWitnesses: 2*(-3)^(1/2) has no real value, so s is not a real-valued function on all R
a=0 would also fail to define the usual real exponential function on all R; the intended a>0 condition excludes it.

cubicGeneralArgument.strictIncrease: For x>y, x-y>0 and Q=x^2+x*y+y^2=((x+y)^2+x^2+y^2)/2>0. Q could be zero only for x=y=0, impossible under x>y. Hence x^3-y^3>0.
cubicGeneralArgument.decisiveDerivative: fprime(0)=kprime(0)=0 although f is strictly increasing and k strictly decreasing.
cubicGeneralArgument.noExtremum: For every epsilon>0, f(-epsilon)=-epsilon^3<0=f(0)<epsilon^3=f(epsilon). Thus every neighborhood contains values on both sides of f(0).
cubicGeneralArgument.correctDirectApplication: On [1,3], u=x^2 and v=-x^2 are continuous and differentiable. For every x in (1,3), uprime=2x>0 and vprime=-2x<0, giving strict increase/decrease on [1,3].
cubicGeneralArgument.negativeTest: A derivative equal to zero at one point does not force a local extremum. Two isolated sample values alone would not prove a general no-extremum claim without a neighborhood argument; the supplied solution gives the required general signs.

visualInspection.finding: Both equally scaled panels show the correct values for 3*2^x and 3*(1/2)^x from -2 to 2, common intercept 3, the correct positive growth/decay shapes and no crossing of y=0. The wording about increasing/decreasing is localized to the displayed positive coefficients; it does not override the negative-coefficient cases in the task. The PDF title, formula exponents, labels and linked prerequisite section are visible and legible.

The two sign directions are correctly displayed on interval I. The cubic crosses the origin with a horizontal tangent and is correctly identified as strictly increasing although its derivative at 0 is zero. The prominent nonconverse sentence expressly concerns strict positivity. Formulas, prime marks and the entire image are legible in the actual PDF. The picture illustrates the increasing counterexample; the assessment separately requires the decreasing counterpart.

78238608-aaaa-4d12-a9de-54f325e9cf6f: Any mathematically equivalent order or limit notation, correct alternative control points and intelligible own hand sketches satisfy the same requirements.

f76d00dc-6b31-59cd-b01a-3610eadc9908: The optional factorization is a scaffold, not a mandatory word-for-word proof. Any valid noncircular proof of strict cubic increase is equivalent.
An order-reversal argument k=-f is the same mathematical content as the negative sign of k(x)-k(y).
For no extremum, arbitrary positive epsilon or the general left/right sign argument is valid. No particular pair of numerical samples is mandatory.
Strictly increasing/decreasing wording, correct inequalities or equivalent rigorous prose are interchangeable; the essential strictness and quantifiers must be evident.
